name: Península Valdés
tagline: A windswept peninsula on the Patagonian coast where southern right whales calve, orcas hunt sea lions from the beach and elephant seals and penguins gather in their thousands.
highlight: A southern right whale mother and calf surfacing beside your boat in the calm waters of Golfo Nuevo.
shortDescription: One of the best wildlife-watching places in the Americas: whales from June to December, elephant seals, sea lions, penguins, guanacos and, at the right tide, hunting orcas, all in a UNESCO-listed reserve.
metaDescription: A Península Valdés travel guide: whale watching from Puerto Pirámides, Punta Norte orcas, elephant seals, Punta Tombo penguins, Gaiman Welsh tea, best time for whales, how to get there and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Puerto Madryn (PMY), or Trelew (REL); the reserve is about 1.5 hours from Puerto Madryn
knownFor: Southern right whales, orcas, elephant seals, penguins, sea lions
goodFor: Wildlife, whale watching, photography, road trips

image.alt: A southern right whale swimming near the surface off Península Valdés

intro: Península Valdés is a large peninsula on the coast of Chubut province, in Patagonia, almost an island, connected to the mainland by a narrow isthmus. UNESCO inscribed it in 1999 as a site of outstanding marine and coastal wildlife. Its sheltered gulfs, cliffs and beaches provide breeding grounds for a range of marine mammals and seabirds, and its steppe holds guanacos, maras (Patagonian hares) and rheas.

The star attraction is the southern right whale, which comes to the calm waters of Golfo Nuevo, near the village of Puerto Pirámides, to mate and give birth, from about June to December, and is most abundant in September and October. Boat trips from Puerto Pirámides bring visitors alongside the whales, which are curious and often approach the boats. Other highlights include elephant seals on the beaches, sea lion colonies, Magellanic penguins in nearby colonies and, at Punta Norte, orcas that famously beach themselves in a hunting technique, catching sea lion pups in the surf, most often between February and April.

The reserve is remote and windswept, and best explored by car or a tour. Puerto Madryn, a modern coastal town, is the usual base, about 100 km from Puerto Pirámides. To the south, Punta Tombo has one of the largest colonies of Magellanic penguins in the world, and the Welsh-founded towns of Gaiman and Trelew give a taste of Patagonia's Welsh heritage, including tea houses.

whyVisit.intro: Valdés is one of the best places in the world to see marine wildlife, and highly accessible.

points.title: Southern right whales
points.text: Close encounters with mothers and calves from boats in calm bays.

points.title: Orcas and elephant seals
points.text: Rare behaviour on view at Punta Norte, and giant seals on beaches.

points.title: Penguins
points.text: Huge colonies of Magellanic penguins from September to March.

points.title: Welsh heritage
points.text: Gaiman's tea houses and chapels, a legacy of Welsh settlers in 1865.

attractionsIntro: The main sights are around the peninsula, with a day for penguins to the south.

attractions.name: Puerto Pirámides and whale watching

image.alt: The small village of Puerto Pirámides beside the bay on Península Valdés

attractions.text: The only settlement on the peninsula, where whale-watching boats leave from the beach. Tours last about 1.5 hours, and run from June to December.

attractions.name: Southern right whales

image.file: File:Southern right whale caudal fin-2 no sky.JPG
image.alt: The tail of a southern right whale rising above the water

attractions.text: Adult whales, mothers and calves are seen at close range in Golfo Nuevo, with tail slaps and breaches.
attractions.tip: Bring a jacket, and keep your camera ready.

attractions.name: Punta Norte and orcas

image.alt: A view along the shore at Punta Norte, where orcas hunt sea lions

attractions.text: A sea lion colony where orcas rush onto the beach to catch pups, an extraordinary hunting behaviour. Sightings are best at high tide from February to April, and are not guaranteed.
attractions.tip: Check tide times and be patient.

attractions.name: Punta Delgada and Caleta Valdés
attractions.text: Colonies of elephant seals, sea lions and penguins, with beaches and cliffs, on the eastern coast.
attractions.tip: Visit in September and October for elephant seal pups.

attractions.name: Punta Tombo penguin colony

image.file: File:Magellanic Penguin Colony ,Punta Tombo - Flickr - gailhampshire.jpg
image.alt: A large colony of Magellanic penguins at Punta Tombo

attractions.text: About 200 km south of Puerto Madryn, the largest mainland colony of Magellanic penguins, open from September to March, where visitors walk along paths among nesting birds.
attractions.tip: A full-day trip from Puerto Madryn.

attractions.name: Gaiman and the Welsh tea houses

image.alt: A Welsh tea house in the town of Gaiman in Chubut

attractions.text: A small town founded by Welsh settlers in the 19th century, with tea houses serving cakes, scones and tea in a Welsh tradition.

thingsToDoIntro: Wildlife dominates, with time for scenery and local culture.

thingsToDo.title: Go whale watching
thingsToDo.text: Take a boat from Puerto Pirámides, between June and December.

thingsToDo.title: Look for orcas at Punta Norte
thingsToDo.text: Wait at the viewing platform for a chance to see orcas hunting.
thingsToDo.tip: Go from February to April at high tide.

thingsToDo.title: Walk among penguins
thingsToDo.text: At Punta Tombo and Cabo Dos Bahías.

thingsToDo.title: Drive the reserve loop
thingsToDo.text: See guanacos, maras and seabirds from the road.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel or dive with sea lions
thingsToDo.text: From Puerto Madryn or Puerto Pirámides, with licensed operators.

foodIntro: Food here is seafood and Patagonian lamb, with Welsh influences in Gaiman.

foods.name: Fresh seafood
foods.text: Fish, shellfish, scallops and squid, from the Atlantic.

foods.name: Cordero patagónico
foods.text: Lamb, cooked on an open fire.

foods.name: Welsh tea and cakes
foods.text: Scones, cakes and tea served with jam and cream.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Puerto Madryn for choice, or Puerto Pirámides for immersion.

areas.name: Puerto Madryn
areas.text: Hotels, hostels and restaurants on the seafront.

gettingThere.intro: Puerto Madryn is about 1,400 km south of Buenos Aires.

options.mode: Flight to Puerto Madryn or Trelew
options.text: Direct flights from Buenos Aires, about 2 hours.
options.detail: Trelew is about 60 km from Puerto Madryn.

options.text: Puerto Madryn to Puerto Pirámides is about 100 km, or about 1.5 hours.
Day tours run from Puerto Madryn.

gettingAround.intro: A car or a tour is essential.

bestTime.headline: September–October for whales, penguins and elephant seals
bestTime.summary: The peninsula has a windy, semi-arid climate. Wildlife follows the seasons.

seasons.text: Peak whales, penguins nesting and elephant seals with pups.
Warm, with penguin chicks, but fewer whales.
Orcas at Punta Norte, from February to April.
Whales arrive, with cold and windy weather.

bestTime.avoid: January to May if whales are your priority.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you see the wildlife.
tips: Go from September to October for whales, elephant seals and penguins.
Check tides for orca sightings at Punta Norte.
Bring warm, windproof clothing, since it is cold on the boat.
Book whale-watching trips early in the season.
Keep a safe distance from all wildlife.
Fill your fuel tank before entering the reserve.
Bring binoculars and a zoom lens.

faq.q: When is the best time for whales?
faq.a: June to December, with September and October the best.
Sometimes, at Punta Norte from February to April, at high tide. Sightings are not guaranteed.

faq.q: How many days do you need?
Can I visit as a day trip from Puerto Madryn?

faq.a: It helps, though tours are available.
